evidence: "check each x has at least one", "used_y", "used_z"; "ncol = 3 * k"; "rows.append((x, y, z))"
affordance_in_statement: For the frequency bands, construct a k × k matrix F where the entry ... is (x_i)^{j-1}. The exact same stability requirement applies independently to the modulation schemes and the encryption keys.
secondary_shortcut_name: bitmask/exact-cover search over three coordinate sets
removal_suggestion: Re-present each matrix as evaluation of the selected values in a dense, fixed, invertible polynomial basis rather than explicitly using the monomial powers 1, x, x^2, ...; this preserves the same non-singularity condition while hiding the immediate Vandermonde interpretation.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that nonzero Vandermonde determinants require one distinct value in each coordinate, then backtracks over x-values while enforcing unique y and z values.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The matrix entry is explicitly given as (x_i)^{j-1}, with the same construction for y and z.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models the task as exact cover with one column for every value of each of the three coordinates.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The three independent determinant conditions, together with values restricted to 1..k, reduce to selecting every x, y, and z value exactly once.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a cached subset-state search over configurations grouped by x, tracking used y and z subsets.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The power-matrix determinant condition is equivalent to pairwise distinctness of the selected values.

common_affordance: The explicit monomial-power matrix makes each determinant a Vandermonde determinant, so the task becomes selecting k triples with all x, y, and z coordinates distinct.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It used the correct distinct-coordinate test but exhaustively enumerated all k-subsets with itertools.combinations, causing exponential running time and TLE.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit entries (x_i)^{j-1} and the parallel y/z descriptions with an equivalent dense fixed invertible polynomial basis for the evaluation matrices, without calling the matrices Vandermonde or exposing the monomial basis.
regression_risk: This may make qwen3-coder's distinctness test harder to derive, but it will not fix its exhaustive-combination complexity if it continues to recognize the equivalent reduction.
